articles.title: Accessing and Configuring Managed n8n Automation
articles.summary: Learn how to log in to your managed n8n dashboard, connect nodes, and execute automated workflows.
articles.html:
Once your managed n8n node is provisioned, you will receive a secure URL (e.g., https://n8n-xxxxx.snbd.media) along with your login credentials.

  1. Navigate to your custom n8n URL in your browser.
  2. Enter the administrator email and password provided in your client portal.
  3. You will be redirected to the n8n canvas dashboard.

Creating Your First Workflow

  1. Click Create New Workflow in the top right.
  2. Add a Trigger Node (e.g., Webhook, Schedule, or On Email Received).
  3. Connect action nodes by clicking the + symbol on the node connector.
  4. Configure each node by double-clicking it and entering required credentials or data values.
  5. Click Listen for Test Event to test, then Activate in the top right corner to run it permanently.

articles.title: Getting Started with OpenClaw AI Hosting
articles.summary: Learn how to deploy and configure OpenClaw secure AI assistant platform on our high-performance USA nodes.
articles.html:
OpenClaw is an open-source, security-focused AI assistant framework. SNBD HOST provides optimized 1-click deployments of OpenClaw on our high-performance USA nodes, enabling you to build custom AI bots and connect them with your databases.

Deployment Steps

  1. Log in to the SNBD HOST client area.
  2. Go to Services -> Order New Services and select OpenClaw AI Server.
  3. Choose your plan and datacenter region (USA nodes recommended for fastest API response to OpenAI/Anthropic).
  4. Once active, go to the server details page to access your OpenClaw panel URL.

Configuring LLM API Keys

  1. Open the OpenClaw Admin Dashboard.
  2. Navigate to Settings -> Providers.
  3. Input your API keys for OpenAI (GPT-4), Anthropic (Claude), or configure a local model endpoint (via Ollama/vLLM).
  4. Start prompting and creating custom assistants.

articles.title: How to Connect to Your VPS via SSH
articles.summary: Step-by-step instructions on accessing your Linux Virtual Private Server (VPS) securely using SSH terminal client.
articles.html:
Before connecting, ensure you have:

  1. Your server's IP address.
  2. The root username (usually root).
  3. The root password (or your private SSH key if key-based auth was set up).

Connecting from Windows (using Command Prompt / PowerShell)

Windows 10/11 has a built-in SSH client:

  1. Open Command Prompt or PowerShell.
  2. Type the following command and press Enter:
    ssh root@your_server_ip
  3. You will be prompted with a security warning. Type yes and hit Enter to add the server to your known hosts.
  4. Paste or type your root password when prompted (characters will not show as you type for security).

Connecting from macOS / Linux Terminal

  1. Open the Terminal app.
  2. Run:
    ssh root@your_server_ip
  3. Enter your password to authenticate.

articles.title: How to Point Your Domain to SNBD HOST
articles.summary: Learn how to point your registered domain name to SNBD HOST using our custom nameservers or DNS A records.
articles.html:
The easiest way to connect your domain is to update your domain registrar's nameservers. This delegates all DNS management (website and email) to our high-performance DNS cluster.

Update your nameservers at your registrar to:

  • ns1.snbdhost.com
  • ns2.snbdhost.com

Note: Nameserver changes can take anywhere from 1 to 24 hours to propagate globally due to DNS caching.

Pointing via DNS A Record

If you wish to keep your DNS management at your current provider (like Cloudflare) and only point your website traffic to SNBD HOST:

  1. Log in to your DNS provider's dashboard.
  2. Locate the A Record for your root domain (e.g., yourdomain.com).
  3. Point it to your hosting server's IP address (found in your SNBD HOST welcome email).
  4. Create a CNAME Record for www pointing to your root domain.

articles.title: How to Install n8n on Your SNBD HOST VPS
articles.summary: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to install and set up n8n, the open-source workflow automation tool, on your SNBD HOST Virtual Private Server (VPS) using Docker and Docker Compose.
articles.html:
Self-hosting n8n on your SNBD HOST VPS gives you complete control over your automation workflows and data. This tutorial will walk you through the recommended method of installing n8n using Docker and Docker Compose.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, ensure you have the following:

  • An active SNBD HOST VPS or Cloud Server with a fresh installation of Ubuntu (or a similar Linux distribution).
  • SSH access to your VPS with root privileges or a user with sudo access.
  • Basic familiarity with the Linux command line.
  • A domain name pointed to your VPS IP address (optional, but recommended for easy access and SSL).

Step 1: Connect to Your VPS via SSH

First, you need to connect to your SNBD HOST VPS using an SSH client. Replace your_username and your_vps_ip with your actual credentials.

ssh your_username@your_vps_ip

If you are logging in as root, use ssh root@your_vps_ip.

Step 2: Update Your System

It's always a good practice to update your system's package list and upgrade existing packages to their latest versions.

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

Step 3: Install Docker and Docker Compose

n8n is best run in a Docker container for ease of deployment and management. Docker Compose simplifies the setup of multi-container Docker applications.

Install Docker:

sudo apt install apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl software-properties-common -y
curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/docker-archive-keyring.gpg
echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/docker-archive-keyring.gpg] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs) stable" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null
sudo apt update
sudo apt install docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io -y

Verify Docker installation:

sudo docker run hello-world

Install Docker Compose:

sudo curl -L "https://github.com/docker/compose/releases/download/v2.20.2/docker-compose-$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)" -o /usr/local/bin/docker-compose
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/docker-compose

Verify Docker Compose installation:

docker-compose --version

Step 4: Create a Directory for n8n

Create a dedicated directory for your n8n installation and navigate into it. This is where your docker-compose.yml file and n8n data will reside.

mkdir ~/.n8n
cd ~/.n8n

Step 5: Create a docker-compose.yml File

Create a docker-compose.yml file using a text editor like nano.

nano docker-compose.yml

Paste the following content into the file. This configuration sets up n8n to run on port 5678 and persists its data in a Docker volume.

version: '3.8'

services:
  n8n:
    image: n8nio/n8n
    restart: always
    ports:
      - "5678:5678"
    environment:
      - N8N_HOST=${N8N_HOST:-localhost}
      - N8N_PORT=5678
      - N8N_PROTOCOL=${N8N_PROTOCOL:-http}
      - WEBHOOK_URL=${WEBHOOK_URL:-http://localhost:5678/}
      - GENERIC_TIMEZONE=${GENERIC_TIMEZONE:-Asia/Dhaka} # Example: Set your timezone
    volumes:
      - ~/.n8n/data:/home/node/.n8n

Explanation of variables:

  • ports: - "5678:5678": This maps port 5678 on your VPS to port 5678 inside the n8n Docker container. You will access n8n via http://your_vps_ip:5678.
  • volumes: - ~/.n8n/data:/home/node/.n8n: This creates a persistent volume for n8n's data, ensuring your workflows and credentials are saved even if the container is restarted or updated.
  • GENERIC_TIMEZONE: It's highly recommended to set your timezone, e.g., Asia/Dhaka for Bangladesh.
  • N8N_HOST, N8N_PROTOCOL, WEBHOOK_URL: These are important for n8n to generate correct webhook URLs. For initial setup, localhost is fine. If you plan to use a domain with SSL, you'll update these later (see Step 8).

Save and exit the file (Ctrl+X, Y, Enter in nano).

Step 6: Start n8n

Now, start the n8n container using Docker Compose from within the ~/.n8n directory:

docker-compose up -d
  • up: Starts the services defined in docker-compose.yml.
  • -d: Runs the containers in detached mode (in the background).

It might take a few moments for n8n to download the image and start up.

Step 7: Access n8n Web Interface

Open your web browser and navigate to http://your_vps_ip:5678 (replace your_vps_ip with your VPS's public IP address).

You should see the n8n setup screen, where you can create your first user account. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the initial setup.

Step 8: (Optional) Set up a Reverse Proxy with Nginx and Let's Encrypt SSL

For production use, it's highly recommended to access n8n via a domain name with SSL (HTTPS). This provides security and a more professional URL. SNBD HOST's shared hosting includes Let's Encrypt SSL, and you can easily set it up on your VPS too.

8.1 Install Nginx:

sudo apt install nginx -y

8.2 Configure Nginx:

Create a new Nginx configuration file for your domain:

sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/your_domain.com

Paste the following content, replacing your_domain.com with your actual domain:

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name your_domain.com www.your_domain.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:5678;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade';
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}

Save and exit the file.

8.3 Enable the Nginx Configuration:

Create a symbolic link to enable the site and test Nginx configuration:

sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/your_domain.com /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
sudo nginx -t

If the test is successful, restart Nginx:

sudo systemctl restart nginx

8.4 Install Certbot for Let's Encrypt SSL:

sudo apt install certbot python3-certbot-nginx -y

8.5 Obtain and Install SSL Certificate:

sudo certbot --nginx -d your_domain.com -d www.your_domain.com

Follow the prompts. Certbot will automatically configure Nginx for HTTPS.

8.6 Update n8n Docker Compose Environment Variables:

Now that you have HTTPS, you need to update your docker-compose.yml to reflect the correct WEBHOOK_URL and N8N_PROTOCOL.

cd ~/.n8n
nano docker-compose.yml

Modify the environment section to use https and your domain:

    environment:
      - N8N_HOST=your_domain.com
      - N8N_PORT=5678
      - N8N_PROTOCOL=https
      - WEBHOOK_URL=https://your_domain.com/
      - GENERIC_TIMEZONE=${GENERIC_TIMEZONE:-Asia/Dhaka}

Save and exit. Then, restart your n8n container to apply changes:

docker-compose down
docker-compose up -d

Now you can access your n8n instance securely via https://your_domain.com.

Congratulations! You have successfully installed n8n on your SNBD HOST VPS and secured it with SSL.

articles.title: What is n8n and How Can It Benefit Your SNBD HOST Services?
articles.summary: Learn what n8n is, its core features, and how this powerful workflow automation tool can be leveraged with your SNBD HOST services to streamline tasks and integrate applications.
articles.html:
n8n is a free and open-source workflow automation tool that helps you connect various applications and services to automate repetitive tasks. It's a low-code platform, meaning you can build complex workflows with minimal coding, making it accessible for both technical and non-technical users.

What is n8n?

n8n stands for 'node-based workflow automation'. It allows you to create 'workflows' by connecting different 'nodes' (integrations) in a visual editor. Each node represents an application or a function (like sending an email, fetching data from a database, or posting to social media). When an event triggers a workflow, data flows through these nodes, performing actions as defined.

Key Features of n8n

  • 200+ Integrations: n8n offers a vast library of pre-built integrations for popular services like Google Sheets, Slack, Trello, WordPress, databases, and more.
  • Self-Hostable: Unlike many other automation platforms, n8n can be self-hosted on your own server, giving you full control over your data and privacy. This is where SNBD HOST VPS and Cloud services become invaluable.
  • Low-Code/No-Code Interface: Build complex workflows using a drag-and-drop interface, reducing the need for extensive programming knowledge.
  • Custom Nodes: If a specific integration isn't available, you can create custom nodes to connect to virtually any API.
  • Data Transformation: Easily manipulate and transform data between different applications within your workflows.
  • Extensible: Being open-source, n8n is highly customizable and can be extended to fit unique requirements.

Why Use n8n with SNBD HOST?

Leveraging n8n with your SNBD HOST services, especially a VPS or Cloud Server, offers significant advantages:

  1. Full Data Control & Privacy: By self-hosting n8n on your SNBD HOST VPS, you retain complete control over your workflow data, ensuring privacy and compliance, which is crucial for sensitive business operations.
  2. Cost-Effective Automation: Avoid recurring subscription fees of commercial automation platforms by hosting n8n on your existing SNBD HOST infrastructure.
  3. Scalability & Performance: SNBD HOST's robust VPS and Cloud environments provide the resources needed to run n8n efficiently, handling numerous complex workflows without performance bottlenecks.
  4. Customization & Flexibility: Tailor n8n to your exact needs without vendor lock-in. Integrate it seamlessly with your websites, databases, and applications hosted on SNBD HOST.
  5. Automate Website & Server Tasks: Automate backups, monitor server health, process form submissions, update content, or send notifications related to your SNBD HOST-hosted websites.

Common Use Cases for n8n

  • Marketing Automation: Automate lead capture, email sequences, social media posting, and ad campaign management.
  • Data Synchronization: Keep data consistent across different applications, such as syncing CRM contacts with email marketing lists or updating inventory across e-commerce platforms.
  • Content Management: Automate publishing blog posts, scheduling social media updates, or fetching content from various sources.
  • Notifications & Alerts: Set up instant notifications for new orders, website errors, server alerts, or customer inquiries via Slack, Telegram, or email.
  • Internal Tools: Build custom internal tools for reporting, data processing, or employee onboarding.

By combining the power of n8n with the reliable infrastructure of SNBD HOST, you can unlock a new level of efficiency and automation for your business.
